recent_primary_claim.title: No bigeodesics in planar first-passage percolation
recent_primary_claim.statement_in_own_words: For iid nonnegative nonatomic edge weights on undirected nearest-neighbor Z^2, if E[min(X1,X2,X3,X4)^2] is finite, almost surely there is no injective doubly infinite path all of whose finite segments minimize ambient passage time. The conclusion quantifies simultaneously over all paths, including paths chosen from the environment.
recent_primary_claim.proof_audit: Only theorem statement and introductory scope were verified against the primary PDF; its 39-page proof was not independently audited in this packet.

prior_attempt.result: Finite geodesics between opposing endpoints may escape every fixed ball; compactness alone does not anchor a bigeodesic. No full-target proof in this record.

working_target: The explicit planar iid nonatomic nonnegative minimum-of-four second-moment formulation of the recent primary theorem; this is a specialization of the survey's broad question.
